prompt: Use case: product-mockup. Asset type: fictional South African stationery catalogue POC product photograph. Create ONE photorealistic studio product cut-out, square 2000 x 2000 pixels, PNG with genuine transparent alpha everywhere outside the product. No surface, no backdrop colour, no checkerboard painted into the image, no contact shadow, no cast shadow, no reflections on a floor. Natural shading on the product itself is allowed. Same studio setup throughout this set: large soft key light from upper left, gentle neutral fill from right, neutral white balance, realistic material detail and proportions, crisp focus throughout, front three-quarter camera view from 18 degrees above unless the subject description specifies otherwise. Centre the complete product/group with its longest dimension occupying 75 percent of the canvas and at least 12.5 percent clear margin, no clipping. Absolutely no people, hands, logos, branding, letters, words, numbers, pseudo-writing, watermarks, stamped markings or recognisable branded product designs. Products and packaging must be entirely unprinted; naturally numbered tools are deliberately unmarked. Generate entirely from this description; no web images or outside references. Subject: ONE plain open rectangular brushed-silver geometry tin with its attached lid folded back, displaying exactly NINE separate geometry tools, each countable and physically complete. The nine tools are: (1) one metal drawing compass with its integral graphite leg, (2) one metal divider with two pointed legs, (3) one plain pale-grey opaque semicircular 180-degree protractor, (4) one plain pale-grey opaque 45-degree triangular set square, (5) one plain pale-grey opaque 30/60-degree triangular set square, (6) one short plain pale-grey opaque straight ruler, (7) one plain sharpened black wooden pencil, (8) one plain white rectangular eraser, (9) one small single-hole metal pencil sharpener. The tin and its attached lid are packaging and do not count as tools. Show exactly these nine tools, with no extra pencils, extra compass parts, extra sharpeners or loose caps. Arrange the tools neatly in the shallow tin and immediately in front of its opening so every item is visible, distinct and easy to count; do not merge or stack the two set squares. All measuring tools are cleanly unmarked: no numerals, ticks, degree scales, brand names or pseudo-text. Realistic thin opaque matte pale-grey plastic, subtle metal brushing, logical compass hinges and correct triangular geometry. Front three-quarter studio view from slightly above, prioritising clear inventory visibility. Critical cut-out requirement: clean fully transparent empty space between the nine tools and outside the tin. No grey or white blotches, fringe, fog, scraps, shadow patches or partially removed background. All measuring tools are solid matte pale-grey so their shapes do not depend on refraction. Keep all tools and the lid inside a generous clear margin. One intentional whole object per tool, no missing pieces.
